claims.text: Infrastructure as code means describing the machines, clusters and services a system runs on in files kept in Git, and letting a tool create or change them from those files instead of by hand.
claims.source_hint: content/glossary.yaml term infrastructure-as-code; opentofu.org docs: Intro (what is OpenTofu / infrastructure as code)

claims.text: scripts/k8s/cluster-up.sh@stage-2 lines 10-19: if kind get clusters lists a line exactly 'donhang', it prints 'The cluster donhang already exists.' and runs kubectl config use-context kind-donhang; else kind create cluster --config deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml; then kubectl wait for Ready nodes.

kind get clusters prints existing kind cluster names, one per line; 2>/dev/null discards the command's error output; grep -q reports a match only through its exit status and -x matches only whole lines.
claims.source_hint: kind.sigs.k8s.io: Quick Start (kind get clusters); bash manual (Redirections); grep manual (-q, -x)

claims.text: kind create cluster --config <file> creates a cluster with the nodes listed under nodes in the config file (one control-plane, two workers here), each from the image given per node.

kind's documentation uses the config file's node list only in kind create cluster --config, when a cluster is created; in Đơn Hàng at stage-2 the only scripted way to apply an edited node list is cluster-down.sh then cluster-up.sh.
claims.source_hint: kind.sigs.k8s.io: Configuration (Nodes; used with kind create cluster --config); examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/cluster-down.sh, cluster-up.sh at stage-2

claims.text: kind delete cluster removes every node container of the cluster, so every object that ran in it is lost, including the db Pod's emptyDir data.
claims.source_hint: kind.sigs.k8s.io: Quick Start (Deleting a Cluster); examples/don-hang deploy/k8s/db.yaml (emptyDir) at stage-2; kubernetes.io Volumes (emptyDir)

claims.text: deploy/k8s/kind-config.yaml@stage-2 lines 6-14 declares kind: Cluster with three nodes (control-plane, worker, worker), each with image kindest/node:v1.34.11 pinned by the same sha256 digest.

OpenTofu compares the configuration with what exists and shows proposed changes before making them, marking a change that forces replacement; since kind sets nodes only at cluster creation, a changed node list means replacing the cluster. No changes when both agree.
claims.source_hint: opentofu.org docs: CLI tofu plan (no changes; forces replacement); Resource behavior (destroy and re-create); kind.sigs.k8s.io Configuration (Nodes)

claims.text: kubectl apply creates or updates objects through the API server of a cluster that already exists; the manifests deploy.sh applies describe objects inside the cluster; kind-config.yaml (nodes, node image) is read only by kind and deploy.sh never passes it to kubectl.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Declarative Management of Kubernetes Objects Using Configuration Files; examples/don-hang scripts/k8s/deploy.sh at stage-2 (no reference to kind-config.yaml)

claims.text: Kubernetes control loops compare the desired state stored in the cluster's objects (spec) with what runs and act on the difference.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Cluster Architecture > Controllers (Controller pattern)

claims.text: Try it: with donhang running and one worker entry removed from kind-config.yaml, cluster-up.sh prints 'The cluster donhang already exists.', exits 0, and kubectl get nodes still lists three nodes, one control-plane and two workers.
Describing each deployment environment's infrastructure in files lets a second environment be made like the first, when the same files are applied to it.
